newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon expected to sell $2.5 bln in debt.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon expected to sell $2.5 bln in debt.

text.p: Raytheon Co is expected to sell $2.5 billion in a three-tranche debt offering via Morgan Stanley & Co next week, dealers said on Tuesday.
The offering is expected to include five-year, 10-year and 30-year maturities, dealers said.

Other underwriters on the deal include Bear Stearns Cos Inc, Credit Suisse First Boston, Merrill Lynch & Co, JP Morgan Securities Inc, Goldman Sachs & Co, Salomon Brothers and Chase Securities, dealers said.
Raytheon Co recently completed the purchase of Texas Instruments Inc's defense and electronics unit for $2.95 billion.
The unit is a premier supplier of advanced defense systems, including precision-guided weapons, airborne radar and night vision systems.

Raytheon, headquartered in Lexington, Massachusetts, is an international, high technology company which operates in several businesses: commercial and defense electronics, engineering and construction, aircraft and major appliances.
